name: Summit Registry

text: Behind the desk, a pair of doors twenty feet high, shut, and polished
where a great many people have leaned on them and been asked not to.
Beyond them the Ascent begins, and there is nothing else beyond them at all.
The registry desk, and the rule, in letters nobody could pretend not to see:
EIGHT BOND CRESTS. NO EXCEPTIONS. NO SUBSTITUTIONS. NO APPEALS.
There is a second card under it reading WE HAVE HEARD YOUR REASON BEFORE.
The standing list. Every Trainer in Caelora with four Crests or more,
ranked, in a hand that is redone every week.
There are three hundred and eleven names on it and you are not high up.
THE CHAMPIONS OF CAELORA. Eighty-one names in gold, oldest at the top.
The gaps are years nobody managed it. There are more gaps than names.
The last four years are gaps.
A case of the four Masters' standards, one per discipline, unlabelled.
The Summit does not publish who they are or what they use.
A card explains, drily, that finding out is considered part of the Ascent.
A cast of the eight Bond Crests, mounted in a ring, with the Halls named.
Briarbell. Stonewake. Tideglass. Emberfall. Mirehaven.
Frostmere. Skyreach. Crownspire. Five of them are warm to the touch.
A wall of failed ascents, by year, with the stage reached against each.
Nobody's name is on it. That was a decision taken a long time ago
and the card that explains it is the kindest thing in this building.
Training halls beyond the far wall, and a timetable of who has them booked.
Every slot from six in the morning to eleven at night is taken.
The Summit is not a ceremony. It is a building full of people working.
A relief carving of the Ascent: the road up, the four halls, the last hall.
It is drawn from a long way off, deliberately, so that the figures
on the road are too small to have faces.
Reading shelves, free to anybody, of every published Hall record
and every Master's match going back sixty years.
Two people are here reading them and neither of them has looked up.
A book on a stand, open, with a pencil on a string.
REGISTER OF INTENT. Anyone may sign it. It commits you to nothing.
There are nine thousand signatures. The last page has four.
Chairs, and a long window on to a training floor you cannot get to.
Somebody down there is doing the same switch, over and over,
and getting it very slightly better each time.

_plan: The glimpse, and nothing but the glimpse. The great doors are drawn in the wall as a sign and have no warp behind them, because the Ascent is Stage 7 and a player must never be able to walk into a stub. The barrier is a solid counter run with one gap, and the registrar stands in the gap. Everything else in the room is a reason to come back: eighty-one Champions with more gaps than names, five of the eight Crests warm to the touch, and a register of intent anybody may sign.
